title: Medical and Life-Support Protections Quick Reference: Application Channels and Registration Limits
content:
Applications for Medical and Life-Support Protections are accepted through the channels listed for each protection. At most one certification may be pending or active at a time on one service agreement, and a denial carries no waiting period before a new application.

| Protection | Channels through which an application is accepted | Certifications pending or active at once on one service agreement | Calendar days after a denial before a new application is accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | phone or practitioner fax | 1 | 0 |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | phone, online or mail | 1 | 0 |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | phone, online or mail | 1 | 0 |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | phone, online or mail | 1 | 0 |
| Life-Support Registration | phone, online, mail or practitioner fax | 1 | 0 |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | phone, online, mail or practitioner fax | 1 | 0 |

**Channel differences at a glance**

- Phone: accepted for all six protections.
- Practitioner fax: accepted for the Medical Emergency Certificate, the Life-Support Registration and the Critical Care Life-Support Registration.
- Online and mail: accepted for every protection except the Medical Emergency Certificate.

**Limits at a glance**

- The figure of 1 is the same for every protection: one service agreement carries no more than one certification in pending certification or active status at a time.
- The figure of 0 days after a denial is the same for every protection: a new application is accepted from the day of the denial onward.

*Hypothetical example:* an application for a Standard Medical Baseline Allowance arrives by mail and an application for a Medical Emergency Certificate arrives by mail. Mail is a listed channel for the first and not for the second.
